I set up a confidence-based labeling plan for your 300-window budget. Here's where things stand:

**Design (olmoearth-inferencex v1.3.1)**
- Population: 16,384 valid windows on a 128x128 grid (model `OlmoEarth-v1-FT-AWF-Base`, revision a347b15; scores raster sha256 a7c40be9)
- Design: `confidence` — 5 margin strata with allocation [106, 79, 47, 34, 34]; the score only allocates labels, so the estimate stays design-unbiased
- Label sheet: `.../design_scores_8f3527f9_confidence_300_s0_to_label.csv` — fill in `wrong` (1 if the map's class is not what's on the ground) and `reference_class` per window, all 300 in order

Two important caveats until you're done:
- No error rate or interval exists yet — it can't be computed from scores alone. A targeted review set would overstate the true error rate anyway.
- Label every row of the sheet, not just the first ones (the least-confident stratum comes first); the estimator refuses partial designs.

When the sheet is filled, send it back and I'll run `olmoearth_estimate_map_error` to give you the map's error rate with the interval this design earns. Note this design gives an estimate, not certification — a certified zone would need a separate `random` design planned before labelling.
